title: Valid Anagram
oneLinerQuestion: Check if string t is a rearrangement of all the characters of string s.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Valid Anagram problem asks whether two strings, s and t, contain the exact same characters with identical frequencies, differing only in arrangement. While sorting both strings and checking for equality takes O(N log N) time, we can optimize to O(N) linear time using frequency counting. If the lengths of s and t differ, they cannot be anagrams. When lengths are equal, we can either use two hash maps to record character counts and compare them, or use a single fixed-size frequency array of 26 integers (for lowercase English letters). Incrementing counts for characters in s and decrementing counts for characters in t means that two strings are valid anagrams if and only if all frequencies resolve back to zero.

- Step 1: Length Validation Guard — Compare the lengths of both strings: `if (s.length !== t.length) return false`. If the character counts do not match upfront, they cannot be anagrams.

- Step 2: Frequency Counter Allocation — Initialize a fixed-size integer array of length 26 initialized with zeros: `const count = new Array(26).fill(0)`. (Alternatively, initialize a dynamic hash map if the character set includes arbitrary Unicode characters).

- Step 3: Simultaneous Frequency Tracking — Iterate through the strings from index `i = 0` to `s.length - 1`. For each index, increment the count for character `s[i]` and decrement the count for character `t[i]`: `count[s.charCodeAt(i) - 97]++` and `count[t.charCodeAt(i) - 97]--`.

- Step 4: Balanced Counts Verification — After iterating through both strings, inspect every entry in the frequency array: `for (const val of count) { if (val !== 0) return false; }`. Any non-zero value indicates a surplus or deficit of that character in one of the strings.

- Step 5: Termination & Final Return — If all positions in the frequency counter evaluate to zero, both strings possess identical character compositions. Return `true`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) where N is the length of the strings, requiring a single linear pass to tally character frequencies and a constant-size sweep over 26 buckets. Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space when using a fixed array of size 26 for lowercase English letters (or O(U) where U is the number of unique characters if using a dynamic hash map for generalized Unicode).
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION isAnagram(s, t):
    IF LENGTH(s) != LENGTH(t) THEN RETURN False
    countS = EMPTY_MAP(), countT = EMPTY_MAP()
    FOR i FROM 0 TO LENGTH(s) - 1 DO:
        countS[s[i]] = countS[s[i]] + 1
        countT[t[i]] = countT[t[i]] + 1
    END FOR
    RETURN countS == countT
END FUNCTION
